comments.author: @amazoncharlie5087
comments.text: My husband and I had a tough few months (like everyone, struggling in this economy) - have cut back on all kinds of things - no dining out - budgeting on evetything -  but after some personal tragedies, we decided to treat ourselves to a special event - watching a string quartet perform Vivaldi's Four Seasons at a local theater in Fort Lauderdale  TIckets weren't cheap (we paid $127 for two tickets) but we wanted good seats, as most likely we won't be doing anything  like this for a while - we got nicely dressed up and it was absolutely WONDERFUL, the quartet were amazing - the theater was lit up with hundreds and hundreds of candles (battery candles of course) - it was stunning.  HOWEVER we were gobsmacked at the end, after their final piece, after the applause, when the quartet thanked the audience for coming and said "There's a tip jar in the foyer, tips would be appreciated, they will be divided equally between the four of us."  I mean, SERIOUSLY?  It lowered the tone COMPLETELY.  I understand the theater will take a large part of the income (after all, it's their venue that they rent out to these events) - so I don't know how much money the quartet will make, but it went from being a charming, cultural evening and a really PERFECT evening, to a much lower class "diner" event.  We were horrified.  A classical concert - being asked for TIPS.  Well I never.
